title: Light: Reflection and Refraction - Worksheet 1
topic: Properties of Mirrors, Reflection, and Basic Refraction
subject: Lower Secondary Science

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the nature of an image formed by a flat plane mirror?
options: Real, inverted, and larger than the object
Virtual, upright, and the same size as the object
Real, upright, and smaller than the object
Virtual, inverted, and larger than the object
questions.explanation: A plane mirror always forms an image that is virtual (cannot be caught on a screen), upright, and the exact same size as the object.

questions.question: A student stands 4 meters away from a vertical plane mirror. What is the total distance between the student and their image?
options: 2 meters
4 meters
8 meters
16 meters
questions.explanation: In a plane mirror, the distance from the object to the mirror equals the distance from the image to the mirror. If the student is 4 meters in front of the mirror, the image is 4 meters behind the mirror, making the total distance 4 + 4 = 8 meters.

questions.question: If you walk 2 meters closer to a large plane mirror, what happens to the distance between you and your image?
options: It decreases by 2 meters
It decreases by 4 meters
It increases by 2 meters
It remains completely unchanged
questions.explanation: Walking 2 meters closer reduces your distance to the mirror by 2 meters, and also reduces the image distance to the mirror by 2 meters. Therefore, the total distance between you and your image decreases by 2 + 2 = 4 meters.

questions.question: When looking into a plane mirror, you raise your left hand but your image appears to raise its right hand. What is this phenomenon called?
options: Refraction
Upright inversion
Lateral inversion
Dispersion
questions.explanation: Lateral inversion is the effect where the left side of the object appears as the right side of the image in a plane mirror.

questions.question: Why can an image formed by a plane mirror NOT be projected onto a white piece of paper placed behind the mirror?
options: The image is real, so light rays pass directly through it
The image is virtual, meaning no light rays actually meet behind the mirror
The mirror absorbs all the light rays, preventing them from reflecting
The paper blocks the real light rays from forming
questions.explanation: Virtual images are formed where light rays appear to come from but do not actually meet. Because no real light rays pass behind the mirror, the image cannot be captured on a physical screen.

questions.question: Why are convex mirrors installed at blind corners in multi-story car parks?
options: They turn the images upside down to alert drivers
They provide a wider field of vision for drivers to see oncoming traffic
They magnify distant objects so they appear much closer
They block out blinding headlights from other vehicles
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors curve outwards, which allows them to collect light from a broader angle. This provides a wider field of vision compared to a plane mirror of the same size.

questions.question: Why can you see your clear reflection in a smooth glass window but not in a rough concrete wall?
options: Smooth glass causes regular reflection, while the rough wall causes diffused reflection
Smooth glass absorbs all light, while the rough wall reflects it in one direction
Smooth glass causes refraction, while the rough wall causes no reflection at all
Smooth glass bends light away from the normal, while the rough wall creates a virtual image
questions.explanation: A smooth surface like glass reflects parallel light rays in a single direction, which is called regular reflection. A rough surface like concrete reflects light rays scattered in many different directions, which is called diffused reflection, preventing a clear image from forming.

questions.question: A security mirror in a retail shop is curved so that a shopkeeper can monitor many aisles at once. What is the primary reason this curved mirror is chosen over a flat mirror?
options: It makes the images look much brighter
It turns distant objects upside down for better tracking
It provides a wider field of vision to see a larger area
It creates a real image on the ceiling of the shop
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are widely used as security mirrors because their outward curve provides a wider field of view, allowing large areas of a shop to be monitored easily.

questions.question: A dentist uses a small specialized mirror to see an upright, enlarged view of a tooth. What type of mirror is being used?
options: A concave mirror held very close to the tooth
A convex mirror held very far from the tooth
A plane mirror held at an angle of forty-five degrees
A concave mirror held very far from the tooth
questions.explanation: When an object is placed very close to a concave mirror, it produces a magnified, upright image, making it ideal for dental examinations where fine details need to be seen.

questions.question: Under what condition will a concave mirror form an upright and magnified image of an object?
options: The object must be placed extremely far away from the mirror
The object must be placed very close to the surface of the mirror
The object must be viewed under underwater conditions
The object must be illuminated by a single color of light
questions.explanation: Concave mirrors only form a magnified, upright image when the object is positioned very close to the mirror surface. If the object is moved far away, the image properties change completely.

questions.question: Which type of mirror is commonly utilized in shaving or makeup mirrors to help users see fine details on their face?
options: Convex mirror
Concave mirror
Plane mirror
Semi-transparent mirror
questions.explanation: Concave mirrors are used for shaving or makeup because they create a magnified image when your face is near the mirror, helping you see skin details clearly.

questions.question: According to the laws of reflection, if a ray of light hits a smooth plane mirror with an angle of incidence of thirty degrees, what is the angle of reflection?
options: Zero degrees
Thirty degrees
Sixty degrees
Ninety degrees
questions.explanation: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence is always equal to the angle of reflection when measured from the normal line.

questions.question: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror. If the angle between the incident ray and the mirror surface itself is forty degrees, what is the angle of reflection?
options: Forty degrees
Fifty degrees
Eighty degrees
One hundred and forty degrees
questions.explanation: The normal line is perpendicular (ninety degrees) to the mirror surface. If the angle to the surface is forty degrees, the angle of incidence is 90 minus 40 = 50 degrees. Since angle of incidence equals angle of reflection, the angle of reflection is fifty degrees.

questions.question: What happens to a light ray that hits a plane mirror perfectly perpendicular to the mirror surface along the normal line?
options: It bends by ninety degrees and travels along the mirror surface
It passes straight through the mirror without changing direction
It reflects directly back along the exact same path it came
It splits into a spectrum of seven distinct colors
questions.explanation: When light hits a mirror normally, the angle of incidence is zero degrees. Therefore, the angle of reflection is also zero degrees, causing the ray to bounce straight back along its original path.

questions.question: How does an image formed by a plane mirror differ fundamentally from an image of an object seen through water due to refraction?
options: The mirror image is real, while the refraction image is always virtual
The mirror image is formed by bouncing light rays, while the refraction image is formed by the bending of light rays across a boundary
The mirror image is always smaller, while the refraction image is always larger
The mirror image is inverted, while the refraction image is always upside down
questions.explanation: Images in a plane mirror are caused by reflection, where light bounces off a reflective coating. Objects viewed in water appear shifted or altered due to refraction, where light bends as it changes speed between water and air.

questions.question: A person looks straight down at a coin resting at the bottom of a clear swimming pool. How does the coin appear compared to its actual position?
options: It appears deeper than it actually is because light speeds up in water
It appears closer to the surface than it actually is due to the bending of light at the boundary
It appears to be shifted far to the left and flipped upside down
It appears exactly at its true physical depth without any change
questions.explanation: Due to refraction, light rays traveling from the water into the air bend away from the normal. When our eyes trace these rays straight back, the coin appears to be at a shallower depth, meaning it looks closer to the surface than it actually is.

questions.question: In the study of light, what is meant by the term optical density?
options: The total mass of a transparent material per unit volume
The thickness of a glass block or a pool of liquid water
A measure of how much a medium slows down the speed of traveling light rays
The ability of a material to absorb all incoming visible wavelengths
questions.explanation: Optical density is a property of a transparent material that indicates how much it slows down light waves. It is completely separate from physical mass density.

questions.question: When a light ray travels at an angle from air into a rectangular glass block, how does its path change inside the glass?
options: It bends towards the normal line because glass has a higher optical density than air
It bends away from the normal line because glass has a lower optical density than air
It continues in a perfectly straight line because air and glass have identical optical densities
It stops moving entirely because glass is too dense for light to pass through
questions.explanation: Glass has a higher optical density than air, meaning light travels slower in glass. When light enters a more optically dense medium at an angle, it bends towards the normal line.

questions.question: A ray of light leaves a clear glass block and enters the surrounding air at an angle. Which statement correctly describes its behavior at the boundary?
options: It bends towards the normal because air is more optically dense than glass
It bends away from the normal because air is less optically dense than glass
It reflects entirely back into the glass without escaping
It continues straight ahead without any deviation
questions.explanation: Air has a lower optical density than glass, meaning light speeds up as it enters the air. When light enters a less optically dense medium at an angle, it bends away from the normal line.

questions.question: A straight drinking straw placed inside a glass of water looks broken or bent at the water surface when viewed from the side. What is the root cause of this optical illusion?
options: The water chemically dissolves the structure of the straw
Light reflects off the straw and gets trapped inside the water completely
Light changes speed and bends as it passes from the water into the air
The glass container acts as a curved mirror that distorts the straight lines
questions.explanation: The bending of the straw is an example of refraction. Light rays reflecting from the underwater part of the straw change speed and bend at the boundary between water and air, making that portion of the straw appear shifted to our eyes.
